summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Lahdo Traitor 1/11)

data.turoyo: Maḥkəyowa, kul gave maḥkəyowa eli w lan naʕime, əmmowa: "Hawxa w hawxa saymiwa appe w qəṭlənwanne w bəʕǧənwanne ba... bu dexono w ba hne, saymiwanne qaflat, qəṭliwanne, məbliwanne.""
data.translation: She used to tell, very often she told me and the other children that they (the Turks and the Kurds) did this and that to them (the Christians), they killed them and choked them with smoke and so on. They used to gather them in qaflat, (groups), took them aWay and killed them.

rationale: First Infectum-wa box; transitive choking by smoke with plural actor and patient.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) ersticken, sich erstickt fühlen; fig. vor Kummer oder Ärger ersticken, bedrückt sein

data.gloss: (Detrans.) ersticken, sich erstickt fühlen; fig. vor Kummer oder Ärger ersticken, bedrückt sein

rationale: Supply the absent Detransitive sense list. Existing examples already show emotional distress; new physical contexts show that death is not obligatory. The literal image of bursting versus choking remains an editorial question.

data.turoyo: Maṭən ann aḥunone lu Kosa, ḥzalle u Kosa taḥt u Bardawil. Omər: "Mudule, bʕəǧleli, hol d qoyamno."
data.translation: Nun kamen die Brüder an und fanden Kôsa unter dem Riesen. »Packt ihn«, rief er, »– er erstickt mich – dass ich aufstehen kann«.

rationale: Thin active Preterit cell; explicit 1sg patient suffix and immediate current distress.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (84/43)

data.turoyo: Omər u malko fṣiḥ w fṣiḥ w gaḥəx w mkayafle, bale u malla w i emo bʕiǧi.
data.translation: Der König freute sich und lachte und wurde höchst vergnügt, aber dem Molla und der Mutter wurde es übel zu Mute.

summary: The inherited entry has Detransitive boxes but no numbered Detransitive sense list. Explicit Detransitive 1 now covers physical choking and emotional distress already present in its examples; active sense 1 and all its wording remain unchanged.

Reduced bʕəǧno/bʕəǧina and long-vowel bʕiǧ/bʕiǧina are provisionally grouped together. Identical reduced complaints were inconsistently assigned active Preterit Intransitive and Detransitive by readers; no new active box is established from that inconsistency.

Death is not entailed in all uses: current complaints, projected quoted complaints, and 84/43–50 concern distress, while some narratives add mayəṯ separately. The edition's platzen and ersticken do not by themselves settle the literal physiological image.

Affected subjects occur without an external strangler; m- introduces thirst, heat, smell or emotional cause, and ʕal introduces the occasion of grief at PrS 73/103. These Detransitive events differ from active bʕəǧleli with a patient suffix.
PrS 17/30, 28/29 and 33/30 repeat inherited examples cited under prs 39/37, 70/6 and 83/4; no new quotation is created solely to change numbering.
No light-verb or separately lexicalized idiom was established.
Does the livestock use at JTM 1.1/95–96 denote choking, bursting, bloating or more general fatal distress? The supplied German eingehen does not resolve the mechanism.
Confirm whether reduced bʕəǧno/bʕəǧina are Detransitive variants of bʕīǧ, an active intransitive formation or a reduced Infectum. Their common Detransitive filing is provisional.
PrS 31/21: confirm person and mood of bare məbʕəǧ in address to the giant.
Check the PrS citation concordance before altering inherited references.
Can a native speaker distinguish emotional choking from bursting, and confirm which contexts entail death?
Detransitive physiological distress is applied to livestock after excessive salt, thirst and heat. Neither literal bursting, bloating nor a specific veterinary diagnosis can be inferred securely.
